JUKEBOX INFINITY - THE JUKEBOX SONGS FOLDER
===========================================

This file is only a guide. You can delete it - the mod does not need it.


WHAT GOES HERE
--------------
Put your own songs in this folder (TEKKEN 7\TekkenGame\Binaries\Win64\Jukebox Songs).
Supported formats:

  .mp3  and  .wav    - any normal music file
  .wem               - Wwise audio files (e.g. songs from other Tekken games or mods)

Other files (like this one, or Song Loops.txt) are ignored by the Song Browser.


SUB-FOLDERS
-----------
You can create sub-folders to organise your songs, for example:

  Jukebox Songs\Tekken 3\
  Jukebox Songs\Tekken Tag Tournament 2\
  Jukebox Songs\My Favourites\

Every folder directly inside "Jukebox Songs" becomes its own folder in the Song Browser.
Songs in deeper folders (e.g. Jukebox Songs\Tekken 3\Arcade\) are listed in their
top folder ("Tekken 3").
Songs placed directly in "Jukebox Songs" (not in a sub-folder) are listed under "Uncategorized".

In the Song Browser, switch folders with LB / RB (or Left / Right on the folder row).


SONG NAMES
----------
The Song Browser shows each song's file name, so name your files the way you want them to
appear (e.g. "Tekken 3 - Jin Kazama.mp3").


ADDING SONGS WHILE THE GAME IS RUNNING
--------------------------------------
In the Playlist Editor, press X (Refresh Folders) to pick up new or renamed songs.
Press the View / Back / Select button there to open this folder in File Explorer.


LOOP POINTS
-----------
- .mp3 / .wav: set where a song loops in "Song Loops.txt" (in this folder). Without an entry,
  the whole song loops.
- .wem: the loop points stored inside the .wem file are used.

Hold Y on a song in the Song Browser to preview its loop.


RENAMING, MOVING OR DELETING SONGS
----------------------------------
Assigned songs are remembered by their path inside this folder. If you rename, move or delete
a song that is assigned to a stage, the Playlist Editor marks it as a missing file and the
game's own music plays there until you assign a song again.
